_doc: The working set: which documents a session is told to read, which are retrievable on demand, and which have left. Enforced by scripts/check-working-set.mjs. Three states only — working / reference / archive — and an unclassified document fails the gate, the same shape as check-gate-coverage.mjs's wired/UNWIRED/nothing-else.
_why: The board was compacted to 252 lines on 2026-07-17 and regrew to 1,504 within fourteen days across three further manual compactions. Decay implemented as a chore loses to write pressure 3 out of 3 times measured. A budget that fails CI does not depend on anyone feeling tidy.

_states.working: A session is pointed at it unconditionally. Counted against budget.lines. Keep this list SHORT — every line here is read before any work happens.
_states.reference: Retrievable on demand and cited by something (a rule's scope, an ADR, a gate). Not read by default, not budgeted. This is where most documents belong.
_states.archive: Moved under docs/archive/. Out of the working set; git and the archive both still hold it. Nothing is deleted for being old.

budget._linesWhy: Authored lines only. CLAUDE.md is 117; the rest is headroom for a contract that has to fit in a session's first read. GENERATED working documents (docs/handoff/QUEUE.md) are reported but not budgeted — their length is a function of how much open work exists, and budgeting them would punish the one mechanism in this company that turns a finding into work. Raising this number requires an ADR, because a budget a session can raise is not a budget.
budget._maxLogRatioWhy: A working-set document may be at most 35% episodic narration. Logs belong in git log, which holds them better and with diffs. Measured 2026-08-07: the board is 87.8% log by line — this ceiling is what makes that a failure rather than an observation.

logRatioAllow.docs/handoff/QUEUE.md: Generated from data/queue.json. Its `evidence` and `closed` fields legitimately cite commit SHAs and PR numbers, which the line-level log heuristic counts as narration. Re-render, never hand-edit.

docs/editorial/decisions/.why: ADR — a decision of record (ADR-028 §6). Excluded by RULE, not by enumeration: if writing an ADR redded this gate, people would stop writing ADRs.

CLAUDE.md.why: The contract. Loads in ~1 of 108 agent sessions but is the human entry point and the source `docs/contracts/rules.json` cites.
